messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: cmdstan and stan submodule
parts:
[renamed subject and moved to stan-dev]

Hi Bob,

Not exactly sure what you've done. Within cmdstan/stan, does "git status" show as no changes? I'm not a master at this git submodule stuff yet -- that's why Jenkins gets into fits every once in a while.

More below.

On Mon, Aug 11, 2014 at 1:42 PM, Bob Carpenter <notifi...@github.com> wrote:
I was just looking at

https://github.com/stan-dev/cmdstan/wiki/Getting-Started-with-CmdStan

trying to dig myself out of the hole I've dug myself into
with cmdstan and the stan submodule. I change branches when
cd-ed into cmdstan/stan by updating stan. Then things got
out of synch in a way I don't know how to fix.

I tried the stan-update:

~/cmdstan(develop)$ make stan-update
git submodule init
git submodule update
Submodule path 'stan': checked out 'a9d4bf373762f40fa89463d0dab8b57ef8c54332'


and now I get:

~/cmdstan(develop)$ git status
# On branch develop
# Your branch is ahead of 'origin/develop' by 5 commits.
# (use "git push" to publish your local commits)
#
# Changes not staged for commit:
# (use "git add <file>..." to update what will be committed)
# (use "git checkout -- <file>..." to discard changes in working directory)
# (commit or discard the untracked or modified content in submodules)
#
# modified: stan (modified content)
#
no changes added to commit (use "git add" and/or "git commit -a")


It tells me my subproject commit is "dirty"!


I've never seen that. If you want to set it back to where cmdstan expects the stan submodule to be, there's a different target:
'make stan-revert'

That *should* set the stan submodule back to the commit.

 
~/cmdstan(develop)$ git diff
diff --git a/stan b/stan
--- a/stan
+++ b/stan
@@ -1 +1 @@
-Subproject commit a9d4bf373762f40fa89463d0dab8b57ef8c54332
+Subproject commit a9d4bf373762f40fa89463d0dab8b57ef8c54332-dirty


Is this just some kind of merge bubble that I should commit, or is there
some other way to back out of the mess I've made?

So... try 'make stan-revert' and see if that gets you out of this weird bind. If that doesn't work and you're ok with nuking the stan folder, 'rm -rf stan; make stan-update' is the worst case scenario, but it'll get things back to normal.
 

And for the future, I should always be checking in and out for the
submodule from the top-level using the make commands?

Not necessary. The commands at the cmdstan level were just for convenience. I think you've been using it correctly.
 

- Bob


Hopefully that helps. If you're still stuck, let me know and I'll try to get you out of whatever bind you're in.


Daniel

parts:
On Mon, Aug 11, 2014 at 2:10 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
OK, I think I'll need a refresher course when I'm back, because
I'm not sure what I should be doing with the submodule.
Sure. Let's also update doc on the submodules (if it exists) while we're at it.

Another question --- should cmdstan always be up-to-date with stan's
develop branch?  Sometimes the above happens, but then it resolves
itself, presumably when someone updates the version of stan in cmdstan.

Unfortunately, it can't always be up-to-date. That would require: 1) pushes to CmdStan with every push to Stan and 2) every push to Stan being 100% compatible with CmdStan.

We can talk about that when we meet up.
